title: Alignment via Generalization
abstract: arXiv:2610.34242v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems can become better at achieving the goals we give them without becoming better at doing what we actually want. Studying this alignment problem rigorously requires a framework connecting measurable performance to intended behavior. We propose Aligned-PAC learning, whose central idea is to reduce alignment to generalization: does success on the requirements used for training extend to requirements the system has not encountered? Rather than express our entire intention through a single training objective, we represent its different aspects through a collection of specific requirements. This perspective already yields strong theoretical results. We show how independent evaluation can provide rigorous evidence of alignment across the represented requirements, and establish how much evaluation is needed. translated_abstract: AI系统可以在实现我们给定的目标方面越来越好，却未必更善于做我们真正想要的事情。要严格研究这一对齐问题，需要一个将可测量的性能与预期行为联系起来的框架。我们提出了“对齐PAC学习”，其核心思想是将对齐问题归约为泛化问题：在训练所用需求上取得的成功，能否扩展到系统未曾遇到过的需求？我们不再通过单一训练目标来表达全部意图，而是通过一组具体需求来表示意图的不同方面。这一视角已经产生了强有力的理论结果。我们展示了独立评估如何为所表示的全部需求提供严格的对齐证据，并确定了所需的评估量。我们还开发了一种优化方法，在明确假设下，通过组合学习到的模型来满足训练需求。
tldr: 本文提出“对齐PAC学习”框架，将对齐问题归约为泛化问题——用一组具体需求而非单一训练目标来表示人类意图，并从理论上证明了独立评估可以为跨需求的对齐提供严格证据。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Aligned-PAC learning, which reduces alignment to generalization by representing human intention as a collection of specific requirements rather than a single training objective, and theoretically establishes how independent evaluation can provide rigorous evidence of alignment across those requirements.
